issues.title: [cherry-pick][release/v0.32.0] Backport FlashInfer fullgraph fix (batch 6)
issues.body:
## Purpose

Backport the merged FlashInfer fullgraph fix #4989 (`7266b8bd2f0058645aaa44d53de108e7cc66c999`) for v0.32.0 milestone issue #4988. This is **batch 6**, based on release commit `ab216c0baefdc49a7a65aeffcd18b995e5e18f3b`.

FlashInfer's stateful/JIT helpers cannot be traced by `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`, which is the default for DreamZero. The backport places these operations behind the upstream custom-op boundary and carries its regression tests. All three changed files match the merged upstream fix exactly. Backend selection and deployment defaults are unchanged.

## Batch selection

Audited 106 issues from the milestone board inventory and its GitHub reconciliation, including issue bodies, comments, and cross-referenced PRs. Evaluated 220 PR-number references. Seven were unrelated number collisions or external-repository references; 213 were vLLM-Omni related/contextual PRs. Checked complete release ancestry and existing squash backports. Batch scope is limited to merged upstream fixes.

| Decision | Count | Reason |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Include | 1 | #4989 is merged upstream and its fix is absent from release |
| Exclude | 79 | Already in release history or an existing merged backport |
| Exclude | 93 | Still open, including 3 existing standalone release PRs |
| Keep separate | 1 | #8448 merged during the audit; its dedicated release backport #9335 already exists |
| Exclude | 38 | Closed without merging |
| Exclude | 1 | #9344 provides comparison guidance and explicitly does not fix #8637 |
| Exclude | 7 | External-repository references, unrelated number collisions, or traceback comments |

### Included source PR

| Source | Milestone issue | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #4989 | #4988 | Restore fullgraph compatibility for the FlashInfer attention backend |

Open standalone release backports are kept separate: #9335 (prompt IDs), #9377 (chunk interactions), and #9381 (Ref2VA documentation follow-up).

## Contributor intent

This batch follows the existing v0.32.0 milestone backport scope: bring missing accepted fixes to release users. The selected failure, affected users, and fix rationale are documented by the original contributors in #4988 and #4989: DreamZero users need FlashInfer to work with its default fullgraph compilation; the upstream custom-op boundary keeps untraceable JIT/stateful helpers outside Dynamo tracing. No new model, configuration option, or performance claim is introduced.

## Validation

- Exact upstream patch, with `-x` provenance and maintainer DCO sign-off; no conflict adaptations.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks passed, including mypy, test marks, SPDX, forbidden imports, and the `torch.cuda` ratchet.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Actual CUDA red/green reproduction on one L20X: release-base FlashInfer fails `fullgraph=True` with Dynamo `Unsupported` at the disabled stateful wrapper; the backport compiles successfully and its result matches eager output. The same runtime, input shapes, dtype, seed, and backend were used on both sides.
- Focused attention/compile/capability/config suite: **171 passed, 1 skipped** (the skipped test specifically requires A100/SM80), on vLLM 0.32.0, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Python 3.12.13, and one NVIDIA L20X. Command: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=5 OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 python -m pytest -o addopts= -q tests/diffusion/attention/test_flashinfer_attn.py tests/diffusion/attention/test_flashinfer_attn_compile.py tests/diffusion/attention/test_attention_capabilities.py tests/diffusion/attention/test_attention_config.py`. Repository xdist options were cleared for this serial run because pytest-xdist is not installed locally.
- Full DreamZero model serving and Buildkite platform CI have not been run for this batch.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex audited issue/PR links and release coverage, prepared the backport, and performed validation and self-review.

issues.title: [Bugfix][Qwen-Image-2.1] Reuse the decode graph warm-up stream per device
issues.body:
## Purpose
Serving Qwen-Image-2.1 with CUDA graph decode grows resident GPU memory without bound as prompts of different lengths arrive, and eventually OOMs (#8750). `max_entries` does not bound it.
Each decode graph is cached under a key that includes `prefix_len`, so every distinct prompt length captures a new graph. `Entry.capture` also creates a fresh `torch.cuda.Stream()` for its warm-up on every call, and cuBLAS keys its process-wide workspace map by `(handle, stream)`. Each capture therefore adds a new key and with it a new workspace allocation — 32 MiB by default — that nothing releases. So the footprint tracks the number of graphs ever captured.
Two arms on the same server, same twelve cycled lengths, 1920x1080, 40 steps, one window from capture #8, where the eight-entry cache fills and eviction begins, through capture #26. Neither arm has any cleanup call; the only difference is whether the warm-up stream is reused:
| measurement | fresh stream per capture | reused stream |
|---|---|---|
| server-side `torch.cuda.memory_allocated()` | **+581 MiB** | **+5 MiB** |
| server-side `torch.cuda.memory_reserved()` | **+778 MiB** | **+58 MiB** |
| client-side `nvidia-smi` floor | **+418 MiB** | **-12 MiB** |

With reuse the cycle repeats value for value, which is only possible if nothing is retained:
```
capture #9..#14 :  16532 16541 16550 16559 16569 16553
capture #21..#26:  16532 16541 16550 16559 16569 16553
```
The +32 MiB per cycle matches PyTorch's default workspace size (`parseChosenWorkspaceSize`, `1024 * 1024 * 32`), and the `(handle, stream)` key of the workspace map (`aten/src/ATen/cuda/CublasHandlePool.cpp`) explains why one fresh stream per capture adds exactly one entry. It is not shape diversity: re-capturing the *same* `prefix_len` three times still grew `allocated` 16422 -> 16937 -> 17321.
### Fix
Reuse one warm-up stream per device, keyed by device index and created lazily. The cache key, the `max_entries` LRU bound, the shared pool, the eviction path and the capture/replay path are all untouched, and the surrounding `wait_stream` pair is unchanged.
I first fixed this the other way — clearing the cached cuBLAS workspaces on eviction through a new `OmniPlatform.clear_graph_workspaces()` hook. That also held the footprint flat, but it clears a process-wide cache that other capture sites share, and it reaches for a private API, when the real problem is that the map key churns. @LinzeShi suggested reusing the stream; the numbers above are that suggestion measured, and the platform hook is gone.
Earlier I also assumed the fix was a missing `empty_cache()` on the eviction path, then a reference leak in the evicted entry. Both are wrong: `empty_cache()` cannot reach a pool held by a class singleton, and `CUDAGraph.reset()` on an evicted graph is not merely ineffective — it leaves the pool in a state where the next capture into it trips a PyTorch assertion.
## Test Plan
**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0
**vLLM-Omni Commit:** `096988d30`
Hardware: single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (96 GB, sm_120), TP=1. Driver 580.95.05, CUDA 12.8 image, torch 2.13.0+cu132, transformers 5.14.1, Python 3.12.
Server:
```bash
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni --port 8091 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --enable-cpu-offload --served-model-name Qwen-Image-2.1
```
`--gpu-memory-utilization 0.3` gives a ~29 GB budget, matching the reporter's total of `4 x 24 x 0.3 = 28.8 GB`, so the model does not fit and is served through CPU offload as in #8750.
### Unit tests
```bash
pytest tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/
```
`test_warmup_stream_is_created_once_per_device` asserts that two captures on the same device share one stream and that a different device gets its own. It fails on the parent commit and passes here.
### Synthetic reproduction
Needs no model and runs in seconds: the same rolling capture/evict pattern with four live graphs, one arm creating a stream per capture and one reusing it.
```
fresh stream per capture:  +384.0 MiB over 12 cycles  (+32.0 MiB/cycle)
reused warm-up stream:       +0.0 MiB over 12 cycles  ( +0.0 MiB/cycle)
```
### End-to-end
24 requests at 1920x1080/40 steps over twelve cycled prompt lengths, then the same workload with a fresh stream per capture, comparing resident memory and the `sha256` of every returned PNG.
## Test Result
```
pytest tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/   ->  93 passed
```
Regression test, on the branch and on the parent commit:
```
# branch
15 passed in 1.86s
# parent commit, with only the test file applied
FAILED ...::test_warmup_stream_is_created_once_per_device
1 failed, 14 passed
```
Correctness: all 25 returned PNGs are byte-identical between the two arms (`sha256` of the decoded PNG), so reusing the warm-up stream does not perturb the captured computation.
`pytest tests/diffusion/attention/` has 22 pre-existing failures in `test_trtllm_attn.py` unrelated to this change; they fail identically on the parent commit, with `flashinfer/jit/core.py` raising during JIT setup.
I did not run L2; the single-card serving run above is not the official L2 suite. No NPU/ROCm hardware was available, so the device-keyed cache is not exercised across devices, and shellcheck was not installed locally (CI covers it). Two properties are reasoned but not measured: the cache is keyed by device index, so a forked child that captures before its parent still creates its own stream, and reuse is safe because the warm-up is idempotent and the `wait_stream` pair is unchanged. Local pre-commit gates pass: SPDX, forbidden imports, `torch.cuda` call sites, test marks, mypy 1.11.1, Ruff check and format.
AI assistance: I used an AI assistant to help read the decode-graph and cuBLAS workspace code, run the A/B measurements. I set up the environment, ran the experiments, and every number and log excerpt above comes from my own runs on the hardware listed under Test Plan. I have reviewed every change and can explain the cache key, the LRU bound, the shared-pool behaviour and the workspace map.

issues.title: Drop unregistered providers from CUDA diffusion IR op defaults
issues.body:
CudaOmniPlatform.get_default_ir_op_priority() unconditionally prioritizes the vllm_c provider for rms_norm/fused_add_rms_norm. The vllm_c IR kernels are only registered on newer GPU architectures; on sm70 (e.g. Tesla V100) they are absent, so IrOp._filter_priority_impls asserts and crashes diffusion worker startup:

  AssertionError: All providers in priority must be registered implementations.

Fix: filter each priority list against the providers actually registered for that op (after current_platform.import_ir_kernels(), mirroring IrOpPriorityConfig._iter_op_priorities), falling back to native only. On devices where vllm_c is registered the priorities are unchanged.

Tests now derive expectations from the real registry instead of hardcoded lists, and a new regression test hides vllm_c from the registry to reproduce an sm70-like registry on any device.

Validated end-to-end on 2x Tesla V100 (sm70) with Qwen-Image-2.1 TP=2.

## Test Plan
**vLLM Version:** vLLM 0.30.1.dev0 (commit ced6857af)

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** based on latest main (a3d7a0444); originally developed and validated against d9bb1c915 (0.30.0-era deployment on the test machine)

 - Hardware: 2x Tesla V100-SXM2-32GB (sm70), CUDA 12.6
 - pytest tests/platforms/test_cuda_ir_op_priority.py -v on a CUDA machine: registry-derived expectations, the #4964 inductor regression, an sm70-like registry simulated by hiding vllm_c (hardware-independent), and the unknown-op fallback unit test (new, addresses review P3)
- e2e: serve a diffusion model on 2x Tesla V100  (sm70) and run a generation request

## Test Result
- 8/8 unit tests pass on real sm70 hardware
- e2e on 2x V100 (Qwen-Image-2.1, TP=2, --dtype float16): server starts, generation returns HTTP 200 (~10 s/image)

> Experimental, opt-in TeaCache support for Qwen-Image 2.1. Related: #8586; separate from Cache-DiT #9062.

## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?

Add optional TeaCache support for Qwen-Image 2.1, including model-specific coefficient calibration and quality/performance evaluation. This follows the scope described in the [RFC coordination comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/8586#issuecomment-6300278675).

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?

Single-request denoising time, with lower end-to-end latency as the final objective and per-sample image quality as a constraint.

### 3. How will this work move that variable?

Keep prefill complete and reuse the decode block-stack residual when the measured change is small. Model-specific coefficient calibration and per-sample quality gates constrain the approximation error.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Users running single-GPU text-to-image generation and image editing in vLLM-Omni need shorter waits and reproducible evidence for image quality, latency and threshold selection.

## Purpose

Adds a decode-only TeaCache adapter. Prefill computes all blocks and preserves per-layer prefix KV. Conditional and unconditional branches keep separate residuals, reset at request boundaries. Output normalization and projection run on every step.

- Requires inference mode, single-GPU batch-1 request mode, an explicit positive threshold and five finite coefficients. Adds a dense calibration collector and quartic fitter; no model-default coefficients are registered.
- Optional `cfg_rel_l1_thresh` and `skip_timestep_range` control true-CFG thresholds and the eligible timestep window.
- Step/parallel execution, quantized weights, FP8 prefix storage, LoRA and offload are rejected. Whole-decode CUDA graphs are disabled; compiled TeaCache is unqualified.

Updated [feature contract](https://github.com/Qing7364/vllm-omni/blob/97a63f1f52f6e7fbd33665d4f5f1acd003dd85e3/docs/design/feature/teacache.md), [user guide](https://github.com/Qing7364/vllm-omni/blob/97a63f1f52f6e7fbd33665d4f5f1acd003dd85e3/docs/user_guide/diffusion/cache_acceleration/teacache.md), feature matrix, recipe and opt-in serving regression.

**vLLM Version:** 0.32.0.

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** Both A/B arms measured `d7c58503f588bc96f3c7bc01612929fa5b6eb1ea`, containing base `0dde197a078f6ab5be474bc6e201619e37119de7`. Current head `97a63f1f52f6e7fbd33665d4f5f1acd003dd85e3` is an email-only history rewrite with an identical file tree; the evidence retains the measured SHA.

Environment: 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB, Torch 2.13.0+cu130, BF16, `CUDNN_ATTN`, eager, no decode graph, 1024×1024 RGBA, batch/concurrency 1. Model: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1@d26bb61231c349cf6b7896fa83353113880e1ba3`; 50 explicit sigmas `[1 - i / 50 for i in range(50)]`.

Frozen policy: `rel_l1_thresh=0.10`, `cfg_rel_l1_thresh=0.05`, `skip_timestep_range=[0.30, 0.855]`, with the five coefficients recorded in the user guide and evidence.

```bash
pytest -q tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_qwen_image_21_teacache.py \
  tests/diffusion/cache/test_teacache_cfg_branch.py \
  tests/diffusion/cache/test_teacache_cfg_group.py \

```

## Test Result

- **136 native tests passed**, with no failures/errors/skips.
- **32/32 quality pairs passed**: eight fixed validation cases × seeds 2026/2027 × CFG1/4. Every prefill executed all 32 blocks; steps outside the window computed fully.
- **40/40 repeated HTTP PNG pairs passed** the same gates; all 96 POSTs succeeded. Repeats produced identical pixels within each layout/arm.
- Gates: PSNR ≥30 dB and SSIM ≥0.95 for RGB, alpha and black/white composites; LPIPS ≤0.10 for RGB/composites.

Mean HTTP latency ± sample SD of five requests; baseline is matched dense eager:

| Layout | CFG | Dense, s | TeaCache, s | Reduction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Text | 1 | 11.610 ± 0.063 | 8.248 ± 0.045 | 29.0% |

## Purpose

Qwen-Image-2.1 rebuilds the same padding metadata in every transformer layer
during padded cached decode. Eligible forwards now share metadata across
layers, preparing it once per guidance branch.

The tested MI300X workload had **5.07% lower client completion latency**, with
**30/30 paired PNGs byte-identical**.

The model rebuilds metadata from the current mask each forward. Each layer
still gathers its own key/value tensors. The combined changes also include #9317:

- Mark known padding masks to avoid repeated checks of mask contents.
- Cache variable-length attention dispatcher availability, including failed imports.

Metadata reuse applies to eligible CUDA and ROCm FlashAttention decode with
sequence parallelism disabled (SP1). Whole-transformer compilation skips the
preparation. The updated [attention backend contract](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/7ec68ffeddb96216a22589804765e881967c6c8b/docs/design/feature/attention_backend_selection.md#qwen-image-21-masked-attention)
describes the provider and layout constraints. User configuration, defaults,

2. **Target variable:** Per-layer padding-metadata work and dispatcher probing.
3. **Change:** Share current-forward metadata, publish known mask semantics,

## Purpose

Padded Qwen-Image-2.1 batches need a 4D block-causal mask during prefill, but the FlashAttention varlen route accepts only a 2D padding mask. During cached decode, the same padding indices and sequence offsets are also rebuilt in every layer.

This PR includes the 4D-mask SDPA fallback from [#8872](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8872), addressing the assertion reported in [#9111](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/issues/9111), and reduces attention preparation overhead:

- Prepare decode padding metadata once per forward and CFG branch, then reuse it across layers. Each layer still gathers its own K/V. Rebuild metadata from the current mask every forward, including when its contents change without changing its shape.
- Publish the known padding-mask mode to avoid repeated mask-content checks.
- Cache vLLM varlen-dispatcher availability, including failed imports, instead of repeating the probe on every attention call.

Metadata reuse applies to eligible CUDA and ROCm FlashAttention paths without changing the attention kernel or its version selection.

The [attention backend design contract](https://github.com/akshatvishu/vllm-omni/blob/5124e8e0b15b4914a9d38e591b8d7ce596e8b045/docs/design/feature/attention_backend_selection.md#qwen-image-21-masked-attention) documents metadata ownership and eligibility. There are no new configuration options. Padded decode retains its existing eager fallback from captured graphs.

## Contributor intent

1. **Outcome:** Reduce repeated Qwen-Image-2.1 attention preparation while preserving outputs and keeping the implementation portable.
2. **Target variable:** Per-layer padding-metadata work and dispatcher probing.
3. **Change:** Share current-forward metadata, publish known mask semantics, and cache dispatcher availability.
4. **Users:** Qwen-Image-2.1 serving users with padded batches on CUDA or ROCm.

## Test plan and results

Tested source matches commit `5124e8e0b15b4914a9d38e591b8d7ce596e8b045`. The local CPU environment used vLLM `0.32.0` and PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`.

python -m pytest -q -m cpu \

issues.title: [Bugfix][Qwen-Image-2.1] Snap the trailing VAE tile so tiled decode leaves no seam
issues.body: ## Purpose Fixes #8850 ### What broke With `--vae-use-tiling`, Qwen-Image-2.1 renders a ~8-11 px wide vertical stripe with a fixed x position on certain widths. It is +6/+7 luma above its neighbours and clearly visible on flat backgrounds (sky, solid colour, flat illustration). It does not depend on the prompt or the seed, and the untiled path is clean at the same sizes and seeds. Measured with the detector in "Repro" below (base revision, height 1024, seed 300): ``` 1024x1024 -> seam columns 885..893 (+7 luma) 1408x1024 -> seam columns 1269..1277 (+7 luma) 1440x1024 -> seam columns 1270..1277 (+6 luma) 1792x1024 -> seam columns 1654..1660 (+6 luma) 1280 / 1536 / 2048x1024 -> clean (seam falls on the border or the trailing tile is a full window) ``` Disabling tiling is not a workaround for memory-constrained deployments: at 4096x2048 without tiling the VAE peaks at ~74.5 GB per rank (reported in #8850) versus ~24 GiB with tiling, and the caching allocator keeps it reserved. ### Repro ```bash # 1. serve with tiling on (base revision shows the stripe) vllm serve Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni --vae-use-tiling --max-num-seqs 1 --port 8091 # 2. request a width whose trailing tile is clipped (1408 = 384*3 + 256) curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8091/v1/images/generations -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{ "model": "Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1", "size": "1408x1024", "seed": 300, "prompt": "Flat minimal illustration, a small orange planet in the lower left corner, the rest is a seamless uniform dark navy blue background, no text" }' | jq -r '.data[0].b64_json' | base64 -d > out.png # 3. detector: column median vs the median of the columns 6..20 away on both sides python - <<'PY' from PIL import Image import numpy as np a = np.asarray(Image.open("out.png").convert("L")).astype(float) h, w = a.shape col = np.median(a[0:h:2], axis=0) loc = [np.median([col[i] for i in range(max(0, x - 20), min(w, x + 21)) if abs(i - x) > 6]) for x in range(w)] print("seam columns:", [x for x in range(w) if abs(col[x] - loc[x]) >= 3]) # base revision : [1269, 1270, 1271, 1272, 1273, 1274, 1275, 1276, 1277] # this branch : [] PY ``` ### Root cause Three parts, each measured: 1. **The trailing tile is clipped by the image border.** `tile_sample_min=512` / `tile_sample_stride=384` (`autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py:1218-1224`, 128 px blend) place tiles at a fixed stride (`for j in range(0, width, stride)`, `:1569`), so the last tile starts at a stride multiple and is cut off by the border. For 1408x1024 the tiles start at latent 0/24/48/72 and the last one is 16 cells (256 px) wide against a 512 px decode window. The decoder is a causal conv stack, so a 256 px window decodes the same region with less context than its neighbours - a smooth, systematic offset rather than noise. 2. **The seam position is exactly `last tile start + blend extent`.** 72*16 + 128 = 1280 px for 1408x1024 (observed x1269-1277), 896 px for 1024x1024 (x885-893), 1664 px for 1792x1024 (x1654-1660). This also explains the clean widths: 1280/1664/2048 put the seam on the image border, and 1152/1536 have a trailing tile exactly one stride wide. 3. **The merge assumed every tile is a full window whose overlap equals the blend extent.** Each tile used to contribute its first `stride` columns (`:1594`) and neighbours were cross-faded over a fixed 128 px (`:1561`). With a clipped trailing tile that assumption breaks, so the cross-fade mixed a 512 px-window decode with a 256 px-window decode. ### Fix - **Snap the trailing tile back to `size - tile_min`** (new `AutoencoderKLQwenImage21._tile_starts()`, `:1533`) so every tile keeps the full decode window. 1408x1024 now yields starts `[0, 24, 48, 56]` instead of `[0, 24, 48, 72]`. - **Let each tile contribute exactly up to the start of the next one** (`keep = next_start - start`); the trailing tile contributes the rest and is trimmed by the final crop. - **Cross-fade neighbours over their real overlap** (`overlap = tile_min - keep`) instead of a fixed 128 px: snapping makes the overlap wider, and a fixed-extent blend would mix non-corresponding columns. - **Use a raised-cosine blend window instead of a linear ramp** (`blend_v`/`blend_h`, `:1400`/`:1408`). A linear ramp leaves a luma step where its slope jumps as the blend meets a single tile. This was the last residual: after the geometry fixes, 1440x1024 still showed +3 luma; the raised-cosine window removes it (PSNR vs untiled 55.65 -> 61.40 dB, where 55.65 dB is the snap-only-and-linear-blend variant). Both implementations of the same geometry are updated: `tiled_decode` (single rank) and `tile_split`/`tile_merge` (distributed VAE with `--vae-patch-parallel-size > 1`). In the distributed path `grid_coord` changes from `i // stride` (`distributed/autoencoders/autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21.py:68`) to the enumerate index, because two snapped starts can share a stride quotient (e.g. 72 and 80 with stride 24) and would otherwise collide as dictionary keys. *Generated output - Qwen-Image-2.1, BF16, seed 300, 1408x1024 and 1440x1024, the repro prompt above, with and without `--vae-use-tiling`. Illustrative artifact, not a ground-truth reference.* Scope: only the Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE tiling geometry and one regression test. No changes to `enable_tiling`, `_tiled_decode_adaptive` (OOM down-scaling) or `tile_exec`. ## Test Plan **vLLM Version:** 0.31.0 **vLLM-Omni Commit:** `596c816` (base) Hardware: 2 x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (96 GB, sm_120), driver 580.95.05, torch 2.13.0+cu132, diffusers 0.40.0, Python 3.12.3. TP=1 and TP=2. Model: `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1` BF16 (31 GB). Regression test: `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py::test_trailing_tile_keeps_the_full_decode_window` asserts that every tile handed to the decoder keeps the full window, for latent sizes whose trailing tile would otherwise be clipped. It fails on the base revision and passes with the fix: ``` # base revision AssertionError: latent 16x22: decoded tiles with a clipped window {(4, 4), (8, 8), (8, 4), (4, 8)}; every tile must keep the full 8x8 window # this branch: 1 passed ``` Commands: ```bash pytest -sv tests/diffusion -m 'core_model and cpu' # L1 (CI step) pytest -sv tests/diffusion/distributed -m 'core_model and cuda' --run-level core_model # L2-style pytest -sv tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py # focused ``` End-to-end serving checks (real service, the repro above): | size | before fix | after fix | PSNR(tiled, untiled) | |---|---|---|---| | 1024x1024 | stripe x885-893 (+7 luma) | none | 54.10 -> 60.74 dB | | 1408x1024 | stripe x1269-1277 (+7) | none | 53.46 -> 59.70 dB | | 1440x1024 | stripe x1270-1277 (+6) | none | n/a -> 61.40 dB | | 1472x1024 | not detected | none | 60.60 dB | | 1792x1024 | stripe x1654-1660 (+6) | none | 55.15 -> 60.00 dB | | 1280 / 1536 / 2048x1024 | clean before | clean after (regression guard) | 56.0-57.4 dB (serving) | The first five PSNR rows are measured on the VAE output (range 2, tiled vs untiled decode of the same latent); the last row is the 8-bit serving figure. The base revision's PSNR was not measured at 1440x1024 - only its stripe (x1270-1277) - so that cell is marked `n/a`; 55.65 dB is the snap-only-and-linear-blend variant and is not used as a baseline here. The height axis is fixed the same way (`starts_height` uses the same helper), which is why 1024x1408 is clean on both axes: no column seam, no row seam, PSNR 60.24 dB. That is also the answer to the issue's open question about why no horizontal seam was seen at 1024x1024 while the geometry is symmetric - the fix treats both axes identically, and the row-wise detector finds no horizontal seam on either arm. Distributed path, activated with `--tensor-parallel-size 2 --vae-patch-parallel-size 2` (probed: `is_distributed_enabled() = True`, `tile_split` entered 16 times = 2 ranks x 8 requests): the same stripes before and clean after, across the same 8 widths. Peak VRAM 29135 -> 29043 MiB, latency +0.1-0.4 s (the trailing tile now decodes a full 512 px window instead of 256 px). Single-rank regression: peak VRAM unchanged (35176 / 36052 / 37674 -> 35176 / 36052 / 37770 MiB) and latency within 2% for 1024/1408/2048. Cost: the trailing row and column now decode a full window, so the decoded area grows 11-44% for these sizes (~0% at 4096x2048, already a tile multiple) and end-to-end latency ~1-2%. The blend also spans more than the nominal 128 px wherever the trailing tile is snapped: up to 480 px for the ~20% of reachable widths whose snapped gap is under 128 px (1312, 1344, 1376, 1696, 1728, 1760, 2080, ...). Those widest-crossfade widths are measured, not assumed: 1312x1024 and 1728x1024 show no stripe and PSNR 60.03 / 59.43 dB. Note that requested sizes are rounded to a multiple of 32 px by the pipeline (1296 -> 1280, 1680 -> 1664), which is why the affected widths are the ones listed above. `patch_size is not None` branch (not used by this checkpoint, which is not patchified): geometry invariants over latent sizes 1..256 for patch_size None/2/4, plus a patched-space check where `tile_split`/`tile_exec`/`tile_merge` reproduce `tiled_decode` bit-exactly (max diff 0.00e+00) with real weights. ## Test Result - **L1** (`pytest -sv tests/diffusion -m 'core_model and cpu'`, 8198 collected, 17:57): 8144 passed, 14 failed, 39 skipped, 2 errors. All 16 failures are environment/platform limits unrelated to this change: 9 x `MiniMax H3 AdaLN offload requires eager CUDA inference`, 3 x `UnicodeDecodeError` (host file encoding), 4 x `Network is unreachable` / `LocalEntryNotFoundError` (huggingface.co is not reachable from the test host), 1 x `FLASH_ATTN ... Hopper-only` (host is Blackwell sm_120), 1 x `Int8 not supported on SM120`. Re-running the same failing tests on the base revision gives exactly the same result (14 failed, 2 errors, 137 passed), so they are pre-existing. - **L2-style** (`pytest -sv tests/diffusion/distributed -m 'core_model and cuda' --run-level core_model`, 5:23): 462 passed, 1 failed, 3 skipped. The single failure (`test_keep_pause_two_ranks_ack_and_rank_failure`) is `httpcore.ConnectError: Network is unreachable` while the test starts an engine that fetches from the Hub; it fails identically on the base revision. - **Focused:** `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_vae.py` 10 passed. - **pre-commit** on the changed files: ruff check, ruff format, mypy-3.10, check-mark, SPDX header, forbidden imports and `torch.cuda` call checks all passed (EXIT=0). actionlint / markdownlint / Buildkite / shellcheck were skipped: not applicable to these files, or their Go/npm toolchains cannot be fetched on the test host. - **Not run here:** the full CI job matrix (Buildkite L2/L3 runners and their SKU marks), other vendors (ROCm/NPU), concurrent / multi-request throughput, the `patch_size is not None` branch with a patchified checkpoint, and the OOM down-scaling path (`_tiled_decode_adaptive`) with the new geometry. AI assistance: I used an AI assistant to help read the VAE tiling code, implement the change and its regression test, run the A/B measurements. I set up the environment, ran the experiments, and every number and log excerpt above comes from my own runs on the hardware listed under Test Plan. I have reviewed every change and can explain the tile layout, the overlap arithmetic and the blend window.

issues.title: [Bugfix][Diffusion] Gate attention-mask capability flags per platform (fixes XPU noise)
issues.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
FIX #6882

## Purpose

`HiDream-ai/HiDream-O1-Image` generates **pure noise** on XPU — exit 0, no warning. `supports_piecewise_spans` was a plain class attribute: `False` on the `AttentionBackend` base, but hardcoded `True` on all three flash backends (`flash_attn.py:175`, `flash_attn_hub.py:85`/`:253`) regardless of platform — and `FLASH_ATTN` is what HiDream-O1 selects on XPU. Only `forward_cuda` dispatches `piecewise_attn` over `AttentionMetadata.full_attn_spans`. `hidream_o1_image_transformer.py` trusted the flag, skipped building the equivalent `attn_mask`, and XPU/NPU then ran **fully dense unmasked attention** — text rows that must stay causal attended to future image tokens. Full analysis in #6882.

A flag describes the `forward_*` that actually runs, not the backend class, so the mask-capability flags become platform-gated `classmethod`s. CUDA / ROCm / MUSA flag values are identical before and after.

- `abstract.py` — `supports_piecewise_spans()` becomes a `classmethod` defaulting to `False`; new `supports_dense_attention_mask()` defaults to `supports_attention_mask()`, which only promises *some* mask is read (several kernels take just a 2D `[B, Skv]` padding mask).
- `flash_attn.py`, `flash_attn_hub.py` — in all three backends spans are `True` only for the CUDA family, exactly the set that reaches `forward_cuda` (ROCm/MUSA via base-class `forward_hip` / `forward_musa` delegation). The hub backends are converted along with the plain one because the base declaration is now a `classmethod`: leaving their `supports_piecewise_spans: bool = True` in place would shadow it with a non-callable and break every caller.
- `cudnn_attn.py`, `vdnh3_attn.py` — the same conversion for two flag declarations that landed on main after this PR was opened (`CUDNN_ATTN`'s via #8099, the new `VDNH3_ATTN` backend via #8439). Both are CUDA-only and keep their old values (`True` / `False`); left as `bool` attributes, every `supports_piecewise_spans()` call on them raised `TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable`.
- `flash_attn.py` — only this backend overrides `supports_dense_attention_mask()`, returning `False` on XPU alone, where its one mask route is `_forward_varlen_masked`, which asserts 2D. The two hub backends inherit the `abstract.py` default and keep reporting `True`.
- `layer.py` — `_run_local_attention` reroutes a >2D mask to the existing `sdpa_fallback` with a `warning_once`, scoped to backends that *claim* mask support so it cannot preempt `TRTLLM_ATTN`'s deliberate `ValueError`. `_assert_piecewise_compatible` now calls the flag.
- `hidream_o1_image_transformer.py` — HiDream-O1's probe now calls the flag. This `()` is what turns the noise into an image.
- `qwen_image_21_transformer.py` — the other model-side consumer, from the same #8099, gets the same `()`. Without it the bound method is always truthy, so `attn_path_hint="auto"` picked `"piecewise"` for every backend — including `TORCH_SDPA`, which then hit the `_assert_piecewise_compatible` `ValueError`.

| Platform | `supports_piecewise_spans()` | Mask reroute | Net effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA / ROCm / MUSA | `True` (was `True`) | no | **No change** |
| XPU | `False` (was `True`) | yes | **Fixed** — model builds the mask, layer runs it on SDPA; verified e2e |
| NPU | `False` (was `True`) | no | **Unverified** — a 4D mask now reaches `aclnnFlashAttentionScore` instead of being skipped, which should be a strict improvement over the dense unmasked run, but no NPU hardware was available. Needs confirmation from someone who has one; see the follow-up on `mindiesd` mask conventions below before assuming it is fixed. |

The reroute fires for exactly one backend on one platform: `FLASH_ATTN` on XPU. It needs `supports_attention_mask()` *and* `not supports_dense_attention_mask()`, and `flash_attn.py` is the only backend that overrides the latter — every other backend inherits the `abstract.py` default, where the two are the same value, so the pair can never both hold. `CUDNN_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER_ATTN`, `TORCH_SDPA` and the two hub backends cannot reroute.

### Scope

Per review, this PR is only the XPU correctness fix: `abstract.py` + the backend flags + `layer.py` + the two model-side `()` fixes. Unrelated fixes that were riding along have been reverted out; the one still open is listed under Follow-ups.

### Reviewer attention

- **The reroute is not HiDream-only.** On XPU, every model that hands `FLASH_ATTN` a >2D mask now runs that layer on SDPA after one `warning_once` — HunyuanImage3, glm_image, flux, flux2 and ernie_image all unsqueeze to 4D before `Attention`. Previously those masks hit `forward_xpu`'s 2D assert, so this turns a hard failure into a working run. CUDA keeps HunyuanImage3's 4D mask + spans on `piecewise_attn`.
- **`supports_dense_attention_mask()` is deliberately `True` on CUDA**, though only *conditionally* honored there: `forward_cuda` honors a >2D mask only via `piecewise_attn`, so a >2D mask *without* spans still hits the 2D assert — reachable by `lingbot_video` and `glm_image`. Returning `False` fixes both but drags HunyuanImage3 (4D mask *with* spans) off `piecewise_attn` onto SDPA, so it is a follow-up. Same for the hub backends.
- **`build_hidream_o1_attention_mask` is newly load-bearing on XPU/NPU.** It was dead code there before this PR, so its test file is new coverage for existing unexercised code rather than for anything this PR rewrites; the function itself is untouched.
- **The 4D additive bf16 mask never reaches `forward_xpu`.** `layer.py` diverts it to SDPA first, so the reverted `torch.any(~attention_mask)` on that path is not on the HiDream-O1 route. Were it ever reached with an additive mask it would raise on `~` over bf16 rather than fail silently.
- **mypy does not catch the `bool`-shadows-`classmethod` regression**, which is how `CUDNN_ATTN` / `VDNH3_ATTN` slipped through the merge. The registry-wide test below is the guard.

## Test Plan

136 new cases: 134 CPU (`core_model`), 2 hardware-gated.

- `test_mask_capability_flags.py` (new, 116)
  - The platform table above asserted rather than described: both flags × three flash backends × five platforms, through a real `OmniPlatform` subclass.
  - The `forward_hip` / `forward_musa` → `forward_cuda` delegation the ROCm/MUSA `True` rests on, and that the flags are callables rather than truthy attributes.
  - The `_mask_needs_sdpa` truth table over 2D/3D/4D masks × mask-aware / dense-capable / mask-blind backends.
  - `_run_local_attention` dispatch with `FLASH_ATTN` on a patched platform, recording which impl actually runs: XPU sends 4D (with or without spans) and 3D masks to `sdpa_fallback` and keeps 2D / no mask on flash; CUDA keeps HunyuanImage3's 4D mask + spans on flash; NPU keeps 4D on flash.
  - Every backend in `DiffusionAttentionBackendEnum` × five platforms answers both flags as a callable returning `bool`, so a future `supports_piecewise_spans: bool = ...` fails CI. Backends that cannot be imported on the host are skipped (`SAGE_ATTN_3` on XPU).
- `test_hidream_o1_attention_mask.py` (new, 18) — rows causal or full at `seq_len` 129 / 1000 / 4231 across bf16 / fp16 / fp32 against an independent `torch.where` reference, asserting the fully-unmasked row *count* and not just the values, since a partially-applied mask writes correct values into the rows it reaches and silently leaves the rest causal. Also `HiDreamO1ImageTransformer.supports_piecewise_attention` over stub backends (all on / all off / mixed), which is the property the pipeline reads to decide whether to build the mask. The 2 `hardware_test` cases build the mask on the accelerator itself and skip rather than false-pass when none is visible; both ran on XPU here.
- `test_attn_path_probe.py` (new, 2) — Qwen-Image-2.1's `_resolve_attn_path("auto")` returns `"piecewise"` / `"mask"` according to the backend's `supports_piecewise_spans()`.
- `test_attention_config.py` — no new cases, only the stubs the flag change invalidates: three `SimpleNamespace` backends whose `supports_piecewise_spans` becomes a callable, a `_mask_needs_sdpa` stub for the one test that drives `_run_local_attention` directly, and a `FlashAttentionBackend` subclass with both flags pinned to the CUDA-family answers so those CPU dispatch assertions do not depend on the host platform.

Each new guard was checked against its regression: dropping the `()` in either model probe, reverting `CUDNN_ATTN` / `VDNH3_ATTN` to `bool` attributes, or disabling the reroute in `layer.py` each fails the corresponding tests. Across `tests/diffusion/attention/`, `tests/diffusion/models/hidream_o1_image/` and `tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/` on XPU, the failing set is identical to a clean `main` worktree on the same container (54 pre-existing environment failures, none new).

**vLLM Version:** 0.32.0 (torch 2.14.0+xpu)

## Test Result

HiDream-O1-Image, 2048x2048, `--seed 42`, on Intel Graphics [0xe223], 30.3 GiB each. `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` is required on this box for an unrelated Triton/Intel defect. Timings exclude a discarded warm-up generation (first-run kernel JIT).

| TP | Steps | Generate (s) | Peak memory* | Before this PR | After |
|----|-------|--------------|--------------|----------------|-------|
| 1x | 8 | 14.9 | 15.2 GiB | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |
| 2x | 8 | 9.4 | 8.3 GiB/card | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |
| 2x | 50 | 57.4 | 8.4 GiB/card | **noise** ❌ | coherent image, legible sign text ✅ |

\* Peak memory from the earlier run on vLLM 0.29.0 / torch 2.13.0; not re-measured on 0.32.0.

"Before" is `main` at the merge base, same script and seed, re-run on 0.32.0 for all three rows: SSIM vs the baseline is 0.053 (TP1/8), 0.029 (TP2/8) and 0.032 (TP2/50), against 0.49 / 0.47 / 0.82 after.

The reroute is observable in the log — `layer.py:776` emits `Attention backend 'FLASH_ATTN' cannot honor a 4D attn_mask on this platform; running this layer on SDPA` once per run.

At 50 steps against the CUDA-generated `tests/assets/hidream_o1/hidream_o1_baseline.png`, using the same LANCZOS downscale the accuracy test applies: SSIM **0.8174** (passes the 0.8 gate), PSNR **18.577** (just under the CUDA-tuned 19.0), visually indistinguishable. `FLASH_ATTN` and an explicit `DIFFUSION_ATTENTION_BACKEND=TORCH_SDPA` are **bit-identical** (max abs diff 0 over the full 2048x2048 RGB image), which is what the reroute guarantees, so the PSNR gap is XPU-vs-CUDA numerics rather than a masking difference. These numbers reproduce exactly on both the 0.29.0 and 0.32.0 stacks.

- Not covered: no CUDA or NPU hardware, so the CUDA/ROCm/MUSA "no change" claim rests on the flag values being identical before and after rather than on an e2e run, and the NPU row of the table above is explicitly unverified. The same applies to `CUDNN_ATTN`, `VDNH3_ATTN` and Qwen-Image-2.1: their behavior is restored to what `main` had, verified on CPU only.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

Split out of this PR at review request — an independent fix to a pre-existing bug, not needed for the XPU noise fix:

- **`torch.any(~attention_mask)` mis-routes int keep-masks** at four flash call sites (`forward_cuda` / `forward_xpu` in `flash_attn.py`, and both hub backends): `~1 == -2`, so every int keep-mask is unconditionally treated as padded and takes the slower masked-varlen path. Qwen-Image is the affected in-tree model. The same helper should reject an additive float mask instead of inverting its meaning inside `_unpad_input`.

Pre-existing and untouched by this PR:

- **`lingbot_video` and `glm_image` cannot use `FLASH_ATTN` on CUDA** with a >2D mask and no spans. Make the reroute predicate metadata-aware: reroute unless spans are present *and* `supports_piecewise_spans()`. Needs CUDA hardware, since it changes which kernel HunyuanImage3 runs on.
- **HiDream-O1 on NPU** now builds an additive bf16 `[1,1,S,S]` mask that `forward_fa_npu` passes unchanged into `mindiesd.attention_forward`, where every other producer supplies a bool keep-mask — so if `mindiesd` reads it as one the semantics invert. This is why the NPU row above is marked unverified rather than fixed. That path ran dense and silently wrong before this PR too.
- `SAGE_ATTN`, `SAGE_ATTN_3` and `RAINFUSION_ATTN` silently ignore an `attn_mask` instead of raising; they should either raise like `TRTLLM_ATTN` or opt into the reroute. And the CUDA-tuned PSNR threshold in `tests/e2e/accuracy/test_hidream_o1_image.py` needs a per-platform value before that test can gate XPU.

**BEFORE SUBMITTING:** read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and run the [precheck-pr skill](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/main/.claude/skills/precheck-pr/SKILL.md) with the code agent for a self-check against project conventions.

issues.title: [Bugfix][XPU] Fix HunyuanImage3 FLASH_ATTN regression from #9248
issues.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->
**Regression fix.** #9248 broke HunyuanImage3 with `FLASH_ATTN` on XPU, undoing the fix from #9123
(and silently moved HunyuanImage3 from piecewise FlashAttention to SDPA under automatic backend selection).

## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?
Fix the regression from #9248: HunyuanImage3 works again with `FLASH_ATTN` on XPU (and keeps using piecewise FlashAttention under automatic backend selection), as it did after #9123, without undoing the #9248 fix for span-less dense masks.

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?
The routing decision in `Attention._run_local_attention`: whether a call that carries `full_attn_spans` is diverted or rejected by the dense 4D mask check added in #9248.

### 3. How will this work move that variable?
The dense-mask check is skipped when `full_attn_spans` is set and the backend supports piecewise spans, so these calls reach the backend's piecewise path again. All other cases keep the #9248 behavior, and each case is covered by a unit test.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?
Users serving HunyuanImage3 on Intel XPU (and on CUDA with automatic FlashAttention selection). After upgrading to current main, they need the model to keep running with FlashAttention instead of failing at the first request or silently falling back to slower SDPA.

## Purpose

**Regression introduced by #9248.** It added a dense 4D mask check to `Attention._run_local_attention`
(`vllm_omni/diffusion/attention/layer.py`). When the backend reports
`supports_dense_4d_mask() is False`, a 4D `attn_mask` is diverted to SDPA, or rejected with
`NotImplementedError` when the backend was selected explicitly or paged KV is active.

HunyuanImage3's dense prompt-KV path passes the 4D `attn_mask` **together with** `full_attn_spans`.

- FlashAttention on XPU, since #9123 ("Honor full_attn_spans in the XPU FlashAttention path")

not support dense 4D masks honors the spans before the mask. Backends that do support dense 4D masks

2. `test_flash_attn.py`: all pass except `test_fa_vs_sdpa`

This PR supersedes [#8876](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/pull/8876), preserving its original implementation and adding Ascend A5 validation results.

## Purpose

`FlashAttentionImpl.forward_fa_npu` never read
`AttentionMetadata.full_attn_spans`. A model that emits block-causal span
metadata — e.g. Qwen-Image-2.1 prefill — therefore ran **full bidirectional
attention** on Ascend instead of the block-causal pattern, silently producing
wrong results: condition images attended to the future target image and text
attended to image blocks. Because the prefill K/V is written into the
cross-step KV cache, the corruption propagated through the entire denoising
trajectory.

`forward_cuda` already dispatches on `full_attn_spans`; only the NPU path was
missing it.

## Changes

Mirror `forward_cuda`: route spans through the shared `piecewise_attn` segment
plan, so segment construction is identical on CUDA and NPU and only the
per-segment kernel differs. Both segment kinds run on
`torch_npu.npu_fusion_attention`:

- **causal segments** (text runs) reuse the existing shared compressed
  `(2048, 2048)` mask with `sparse_mode=3` (rightDownCausal). `piecewise_attn`
  gives causal segments `kv_end == q_end` in global coordinates, so they always
  satisfy `Sq <= Skv`, and bottom-right alignment reproduces FlashAttention's
  `attn(Q[:, s:e], K[:, :e], causal=True)` contract. No new mask is created —
  this is the same `_get_npu_compressed_causal_mask` the native causal path uses.
- **full segments** (condition/target image blocks) pass **no mask** at all —
  `sparse_mode` is ignored when `atten_mask` is `None` — so they are plain
  bidirectional attention over the truncated K/V prefix.

The operator call is factored into `_npu_fusion_attention` so the pre-existing
explicit-causal branch and the new piecewise path share one call site.

`_resolve_npu_execution_path` now reports `npu_piecewise` instead of falling
through to `npu_unverified` on span metadata. The FP8/MX quantized path already
rejects spans (`"piecewise attention requires the float attention path"`), so
no change was needed there.

## Test Plan

CPU regression on the final revision (`e19cc3d`): **121 passed, 5 deselected**. Tests use mocked NPU kernels and cover execution-path resolution, per-segment kernel/mask arguments, numerical agreement with a dense block-causal reference, both causal settings for piecewise attention, and the causal-without-spans routing boundary.

A5 experiments used the [`quay.io/ascend/vllm-omni:v0.31.0rc1-a5`](https://quay.io/repository/ascend/vllm-omni?tab=tags) base image.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Before | Pre-fix baseline: the NPU path ignored `full_attn_spans` and performed full bidirectional attention instead of the intended block-causal pattern. | `4a910f239079` |
| Golden | Correctness reference: the fixed implementation manually forced to the explicit dense block-causal mask path with `attn_path="mask"`. | `4be8385d4c8b` + mask override |
| After | Fixed implementation using the default NPU piecewise path, following the shared CUDA/NPU segment plan to preserve the intended block-causal pattern. | `4be8385d4c8b` |

These revisions identify the sources used for the recorded A5 measurements. The final revision (`e19cc3d`) additionally fixes execution-path reporting and expands CPU coverage without changing attention kernel execution.

**Shared experiment settings**

| Item | Configuration |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware / precision / batch | Ascend A5 / BF16 / batch size 1 |
| Model | Qwen-Image-2.1, local checkpoint |
| Denoising steps | Kernel profiling: **2**; image comparison: **50** |

| T2I prompt | "A ceramic teapot on a wooden table" |
| T2I seed | 142 (example default) |
| I2I prompt | "Let this mascot dance under the moon, surrounded by floating stars" |
| I2I seed | 42 |
| I2I reference input | `qwen_bear.png`, RGBA; downloaded from the [public reference image](https://vllm-public-assets.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/omni-assets/qwen-bear.png) |
| Saved output resolution | 1024 × 1024 |
| Additional warmup runs | 0 |
| Measured profiling runs | 1 per variant |

Generation follows the [Qwen-Image 2.1 offline examples](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-omni/blob/e19cc3dc49acc5cc7665e09c6b301e6eae792ec6/recipes/Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1.md#offline-inference), using the inputs and settings listed above. Profiling and image generation use the same generation settings except for the denoising step count.

## Test Result

Timings are accumulated device-kernel durations from a single two-step profiling run per variant, without additional warmup. They are bounded observations, not end-to-end generation latency.

**Performance — I2I, accumulated kernel durations in ms**

issues.title: [Bugfix][Diffusion] Evaluate dense 4D attention masks on SDPA instead of the 2D-only flash path
issues.body:
## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?

Make the Qwen-Image-2.1 CI lanes and multi-request serving work when a batch is padded or heterogeneous, instead of failing every such request with `AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)` (#9187, #9111, #8830).

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?

Which backend evaluates the dense 4D block-causal mask that the model builds for padded/heterogeneous batches. FlashAttention's masked varlen path only accepts a 2D key-padding mask, so the choice of path — not the mask content — decides whether the request succeeds.

### 3. How will this work move that variable?

It makes the backend capability explicit (`supports_dense_pair_mask`), and when the selected backend cannot consume a 4D mask the Attention layer evaluates that call with SDPA, which handles the pair mask exactly. Piecewise-span metadata is untouched, so the unpadded homogeneous path keeps using FlashAttention.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Users serving Qwen-Image-2.1 (and any diffusion model that emits a dense pair mask) with more than one prompt, and the CI owners of the Diffusion X2I/X2T perf lanes. They need a batch with mixed prompt lengths to produce an image rather than an HTTP 500, and they need the nightly perf guard to be green.

## Purpose

Before: `supports_attention_mask()` returns True for the whole FlashAttention backend, but `FlashAttentionImpl._forward_varlen_masked` asserts `attention_mask.ndim == 2`. Qwen-Image-2.1 documents two attention representations — piecewise `full_attn_spans` for homogeneous, unpadded batches, and a dense `(batch, 1, q, kv)` block-causal `attn_mask` otherwise — so any padded or heterogeneous batch reached the masked-varlen path with a 4D tensor and died inside the kernel. On A100 that is the reported perf-lane failure; on L20 it is an HTTP 500 for mixed prompt lengths (#9111); with `--max-num-seqs 8` it is the same crash (#8830).

After: backends declare whether they can consume a dense pair mask (`supports_dense_pair_mask`, default False). SDPA, cuDNN and FlashInfer set it True — SDPA evaluates arbitrary boolean pair masks natively, cuDNN FMHA consumes the mask through torch SDPA (verified against the SDPA reference on the same geometry), and FlashInfer's `_pack_mask_for_flashinfer` already collapses the head dim and broadcasts a 4D mask into its `custom_mask`. When a 4D mask arrives without piecewise spans and the selected backend does not support it, the Attention layer routes the call to its existing SDPA fallback and logs one warning. Piecewise metadata is unaffected: the spans carry the structure there, so FlashAttention keeps running that path. An explicitly selected backend still raises `NotImplementedError` with an actionable message rather than silently switching, matching the existing cross-attention fallback contract.

The kernel assert stays as a guard for direct backend use, so the capability claim and the implementation can no longer drift silently.

User guide/example unchanged: no CLI surface, no config key, no model behavior change. The masked result is identical to what SDPA computes for the same mask (the tests compare against SDPA on the same geometry).

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0 (test host) / 0.32.0 (CI)

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** `15bce3458`

- `pytest tests/diffusion/attention/ tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/ -q --ignore=tests/diffusion/attention/test_ring_vllm_flash_attn.py` on an A100-80GB host
- New tests in `tests/diffusion/attention/test_flash_attn.py`:
  - capability flags (`FLASH_ATTN` False; `SDPA`, `CUDNN_ATTN`, `FLASHINFER_ATTN` True)
  - block-causal mask reproducer: the flash kernel still rejects the 4D mask; the `Attention` layer returns the SDPA result with the flash backend never called
  - the same 4D mask **with** `full_attn_spans` still runs on the flash backend and matches the SDPA reference
- Reproducer geometry matches the model: right-padded text prefix (3/40 valid) + two image blocks of 8 tokens, mask `(q >= k) | same_block` minus padded keys.

## Test Result
### End-to-end (A100-80GB, real model, real server)

Qwen-Image-2.1 served with `vllm serve --omni --max-num-seqs 4`, four concurrent requests with **different prompt lengths** (the batch is padded to the longest prompt, which is what makes the model build the 4D block-causal mask). Identical commands before and after the change, only the patch stashed/unstashed.

**Before (unpatched)** — 3 of 4 requests return 500, the mixed-length wave dies inside the kernel:

```
req2 http=200 t=1.96s
req1 http=500 t=5.04s
req3 http=500 t=5.04s
req4 http=500 t=5.04s
{"error":{"message":"Image generation failed: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)",
 "type":"Internal Server Error","param":null,"code":500}}
$ grep -c "attention_mask must be 2D" serve_before.log
24
```

**After (this PR)** — all four return 200 and the fallback is recorded exactly once:

```
req1 http=200 t=19.14s     req2 http=200 t=22.52s
req3 http=200 t=19.15s     req4 http=200 t=22.53s
$ grep -c "Using SDPA for a dense 4D attention mask" serve_batch.log
1
$ grep -c "attention_mask must be 2D" serve_batch.log
0
```

Single-request (batch=1) traffic is unaffected: with no cross-request padding the model keeps using the piecewise-span flash path and no fallback warning is emitted, which is why the earlier single-prompt run stayed on flash.

(The requests are served sequentially in waves of up to 4, so a request that happens to share a wave with same-length prompts — `req2` above — survives even unpatched; the failure needs a mixed-length wave, which is what the CI high-concurrency lane produces.)

Before the change, the reproducer on A100-80GB fails at both levels:

```
[flash] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)
[sdpa] reference OK (1, 1536, 24, 64)
[layer] selected backend: FLASH_ATTN
[layer] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)
```

After the change:

```
Using SDPA for a dense 4D attention mask because FLASH_ATTN only supports a 2D key-padding mask.
[flash] REPRODUCED: AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D, (batch_size, seq_len)   # kernel guard intact
[sdpa] reference OK (1, 1536, 24, 64)
[layer] OK (1, 1536, 24, 64) max_abs_diff_vs_sdpa=0.0000
```

Full suite:

```
1199 passed, 216 skipped, 25 warnings
```

(The two `test_trtllm_contract` failures in the raw run are pre-existing on this host — TensorRT-LLM is not installed in the test environment; they fail identically without this change. `test_ring_vllm_flash_attn.py` cannot be collected against vLLM 0.31 because it imports `RequestError` from `vllm.outputs`, also unrelated.)

## Related

Fixes #9187
Fixes #9111
Fixes #8830

issues.body:
## Contributor intent

1. **What outcome do you want to achieve?** Fix issue #8830 so Qwen-Image-2.1 completes text-to-image generation with the FlashAttention diffusion backend on heterogeneous/padded batches instead of asserting.
2. **What is the highest-leverage variable?** The flash backend's acceptance of the 4D block-causal mask — the exact crash site. A targeted dispatch change there fixes every request on such batches without touching the model layer.
3. **How will this work move that variable?** `FlashAttentionImpl.forward_cuda` already has a masked path; non-2D masks now route to a SDPA fallback, which consumes arbitrary 4D masks natively and preserves the block-causal semantics.
4. **Whose customer or user needs does this address?** Users serving Qwen-Image-2.1 with the flash backend and `--max-num-seqs > 1` / heterogeneous image sizes — their requests crash with `AssertionError: attention_mask must be 2D`.

## Purpose

**What broke.** On a padded/heterogeneous batch, `QwenImage21Transformer` builds a dense 4D block-causal mask `(batch, 1, seq_q, seq_k)` via `_build_block_causal_mask`. The FlashAttention backend's `_forward_varlen_masked` only accepts a 2D key-padding mask and asserts `attention_mask.ndim == 2`, crashing every request.

**Root cause.** The FA varlen path (`_unpad_input`/`_upad_input`) filters query and key with the same per-key 2D mask, which cannot express block-causal structure. The 4D mask is produced exactly when padding is present (`has_padding or sp_padding -> "mask"` path in `_resolve_attn_path`), so single-request serving that never forms a padded batch is unaffected.

**Fix.** In `vllm_omni/diffusion/attention/backends/flash_attn.py`, `forward_cuda` now dispatches non-2D attention masks to a new `_forward_4d_masked_sdpa` (SDPA), which consumes 4D masks directly and preserves block-causal semantics. 2D key-padding masks keep the existing varlen path; the change is confined to the flash backend and does not touch the model layer.

**Repro.** Serve Qwen-Image-2.1 with flash attention and a padded batch:
```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni --step-execution --max-num-seqs 2
# then send two concurrent /v1/chat/completions with different image sizes
```
Each request asserts `attention_mask must be 2D` before this fix and completes after it. The regression test reproduces the 4D-mask dispatch at the unit level.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0
**vLLM-Omni Commit:** 2806b030d

- CPU regression tests (new file `tests/diffusion/attention/test_flash_4d_mask_fallback.py`): `7 passed`. Covers fallback numerics vs exact masked-matmul reference, key-padding variant, the `forward_cuda` 4D->SDPA dispatch guard, and 2D masks staying on the varlen path.
- A100 (A100-PCIE-40GB, torch 2.13.0+cu129): the real `_build_block_causal_mask` -> real `FlashAttentionImpl.forward_cuda` with a 4D mask routes to SDPA and matches reference (`max|out-ref| ≈ 1e-6` fp32); the pre-fix varlen path asserts on the same mask; `_resolve_attn_path` routing (`has_padding -> "mask"`) confirmed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both changed files.

## Test Result

Before this fix the 4D-mask path asserts; after it, the masked forward returns correct output (CPU unit + A100 numeric check above).

issues.title: [NPU] Support piecewise block-causal attention for full_attn_spans
issues.body:
## Purpose

`FlashAttentionImpl.forward_fa_npu` never read
`AttentionMetadata.full_attn_spans`. A model that emits block-causal span
metadata — e.g. Qwen-Image-2.1 prefill — therefore ran **full bidirectional
attention** on Ascend instead of the block-causal pattern, silently producing
wrong results: condition images attended to the future target image and text
attended to image blocks. Because the prefill K/V is written into the
cross-step KV cache, the corruption propagated through the entire denoising
trajectory.

`forward_cuda` already dispatches on `full_attn_spans`; only the NPU path was
missing it.

## Changes

Mirror `forward_cuda`: route spans through the shared `piecewise_attn` segment
plan, so segment construction is identical on CUDA and NPU and only the
per-segment kernel differs. Both segment kinds run on
`torch_npu.npu_fusion_attention`:

- **causal segments** (text runs) reuse the existing shared compressed
  `(2048, 2048)` mask with `sparse_mode=3` (rightDownCausal). `piecewise_attn`
  gives causal segments `kv_end == q_end` in global coordinates, so they always
  satisfy `Sq <= Skv`, and bottom-right alignment reproduces FlashAttention's
  `attn(Q[:, s:e], K[:, :e], causal=True)` contract. No new mask is created —
  this is the same `_get_npu_compressed_causal_mask` the native causal path uses.
- **full segments** (condition/target image blocks) pass **no mask** at all —
  `sparse_mode` is ignored when `atten_mask` is `None` — so they are plain
  bidirectional attention over the truncated K/V prefix.

The operator call is factored into `_npu_fusion_attention` so the pre-existing
explicit-causal branch and the new piecewise path share one call site.

`_resolve_npu_execution_path` now reports `npu_piecewise` instead of falling
through to `npu_unverified` on span metadata. The FP8/MX quantized path already
rejects spans (`"piecewise attention requires the float attention path"`), so
no change was needed there.

## Visual verification

Same prompt, same seed, NPU, multi-reference I2I:

| | Output |
|---|---|
| Golden — `attn_path="mask"` (dense block-causal) | _to be attached_ |
| Before — default path, span metadata silently dropped | _to be attached_ |
| After — this PR, default path | _to be attached_ |

## Test

`tests/diffusion/attention/test_flash_attn.py` gains three cases in the
existing CPU NPU-contract group (fake `torch_npu`, no device required):

- the execution path resolves to `npu_piecewise`;
- a two-segment input issues one kernel call per segment, with the compressed
  mask + `sparse_mode=3` for the causal segment and no mask + `sparse_mode=0`
  for the full segment;
- a four-segment input matches a dense `(q >= kv) or same_image_block`
  reference.

⚠️ Pending: the in-repo pytest run and the Ascend end-to-end result (compared
against the `attn_path="mask"` golden above) are being collected and will be
attached.

issues.body:
## Purpose

Related to #8586 (B2).

Qwen-Image-2.1 requests with the same reference-image layout can enter one batch despite having different prompt lengths. This introduces text padding and makes the batch ineligible for decode CUDA graphs. The B2 experiments also observed larger output differences when the same request shared a wave with longer prompts than when only its wave size changed.

This change adds the templated positive-prompt token count to the model's batch compatibility key. When true CFG is enabled, it also includes the negative-prompt token count. Same-length requests remain compatible. Eager and graph-disabled configurations retain length-agnostic grouping, and checkpoints without an available processor tokenizer fall back to the existing grouping policy.

Prompt construction is shared between preprocessing and encoding to keep the sizing template consistent. The PR changes only the pipeline and its compatibility tests; benchmark tools are excluded.

This is a graph-enabled grouping strategy, not a kernel optimization or a general fix for eager-mode output drift. It trades cross-length batching opportunities for padding-free compatible waves.

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** `0.31.0`

**vLLM-Omni experimental base:** `428758b268cd48334aa57cdead210facb76a6e56`

**PR integration base:** `b164fea797531c1fa10f8b87829632cad006b9fc` (upstream main at preparation time).

**PRO6000 experiment environment:** 1× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell 96GB; Python 3.12.3; torch `2.13.0+cu130`; diffusers `0.40.0`; transformers `5.14.1`; BF16; `CUDNN_ATTN`; no TP/SP or offload.

**Model:** `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1@d26bb61231c349cf6b7896fa83353113880e1ba3`.

The reported validation was completed on the PRO6000 before this submission. The Mac checkout is used for integration and submission; those results have not been rerun against the newer integration base.

Compatibility tests cover text/image layouts, prompt scaffolds, positive/negative prompt lengths, matching and mismatched lengths under RequestScheduler/StepScheduler, and eager/graph-disabled behavior:

```bash
python -m pytest -o addopts='' -q \
  tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_batch_compatibility.py
```

Serving experiments covered short/long prompts, 0/1/4 reference images, reference-image sizes, RGBA inputs and staggered arrivals at 1024×1024 and 50 steps. T2I seed was 42, edit seed 7, and `true_cfg_scale=1.0` except for the CFG validation case. Graph-enabled request mode used:

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/Qwen-Image-2.1 --omni --port 8091 \
  --max-num-seqs 4 --request-batch-max-wait-ms 500 --log-stats
```

The eager control added `--enforce-eager`. Each formal comparison used a discarded full-shape warmup followed by two measured runs. Benchmark harnesses and raw artifacts are separate from this runtime-only PR.

## Test Result

PRO6000 validation reported **42 compatibility tests passed** and **11 serving validation scenarios passed**. These are the completed device-environment results, not a new Mac test run.

- Real same-length batch-2 outputs met the declared PSNR/SSIM gates: minimum PSNR 40.87 dB for T2I and 55.39 dB for single-reference editing.
- Split scenarios matched their respective single-request goldens byte-for-byte, including negative-prompt-length and RGBA cases. Request-ID coverage, output mapping/identity checks and repeat determinism passed in the tested scenarios.
- At fixed wave size 3, homogeneous vs mixed-length context produced 27.66 dB PSNR / 0.96416 SSIM for the same request; alone vs homogeneous context produced 43.98 dB / 0.99624. This is evidence of batch-context-dependent drift, not a claim that this PR localizes its internal source.

| Workload / configuration | Before | After | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Graph-on, 0ref mixed lengths | 0.0657 images/s | 0.0787 images/s | +19.8%; observed run-to-run variation 1.8% |
| Graph-on, 1ref mixed lengths | 0.0623 images/s | 0.0679 images/s | Baseline had split/ragged modes; no definite speedup claimed |
| Other graph-on cells | — | — | No regression detected under the declared variation-based threshold |
| Eager controls, 14 cells | — | — | Within threshold; expected length-grouping no-op |

The 0ref improvement comes from grouping/execution behavior. It should not be extrapolated to all editing workloads, larger batches or other hardware. Whole-device campaign NVML peaks were 94.1 GiB before and 94.7 GiB after; accumulated allocator/graph state makes these unsuitable for attributing a memory delta. No OOM or inference failures were recorded in the final A/B campaigns.

Four-reference requests did not co-batch in the tested setup, even with a two-second admission window; the reason remains unresolved. Multi-GPU TP/SP and 2048² are outside this validation scope. Eager-mode mixed-length output drift remains outside the change's scope.

issues.title: [Bugfix][Qwen-Image-2.1] Drop idle decode-graph prefix copies
issues.body:
Fixes #8831.

## What the report shows

A Qwen-Image-2.1 server started with `--omni --step-execution --vae-use-tiling --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-num-seqs 8` handles one image-edit request, then the next, and GPU memory keeps climbing. After enough requests the process dies in `_scatter_kv_cache` while cloning the prefix K/V. In the posted trace that clone is about 130 MiB, and the allocator has about 27 MiB free. The CUDA graph private pool in that trace is only about 792 MiB, so the memory that filled the card is ordinary tensors, not the graph pool.

Two observations from the report narrow the cause:

- The repro script sets `SHUFFLE=1` and reorders the same four images on every request. Repeating one fixed order does not keep adding a full extra copy.
- Setting `causal_condition=false` stops the growth, and latency goes from about 11 s to about 36 s. That flag is what turns the prefix K/V cache, and the decode CUDA graph that depends on it, on. The default is on.
- The retention fix in #8760 (for #8750) was already tried on this server and still OOM'd. This is a different copy.

## Root cause

`causal_condition` makes the text tokens and the condition images a prefix. After the first denoising step that prefix is not recomputed. Two copies of it exist, and only one of them was being freed.

1. The request's own cache lives in `state.extra["kv_cache"]`. The step runner drops that state when the request finishes, so this copy is not what accumulates across requests. It is also why the cached path is faster than `causal_condition=false`.
2. Decode CUDA graph replay cannot capture the request's tensors, because the next request allocates new storage. `QwenImage21DecodeGraphManager` therefore keeps a separate static K/V buffer per graph key and copies the live prefix into it before replay. The key includes the full `img_shapes` tuple. Each entry is owned by a weak reference to the request's prefix K tensor.

The manager only deletes an entry when the table is full (default 8) and a new key needs a slot. A dead weak reference does not free the static buffers. The entry just sits there, waiting to be reused if another request comes in with the same key.

That reuse is real: the same image order hits the same key and does not allocate another prefix. The shuffle breaks it. Each input image is resized from its own aspect ratio (`calculate_dimensions`), and the generated frame is appended after those shapes. Reordering the four images changes `img_shapes`, which changes the graph key, even when the prompt and the output size stay the same. Request 1 leaves static prefix A. Request 2, with a different order, leaves static prefix B beside it. Both owners are already dead. The copies stay until eight distinct layouts have been seen.

The OOM is one request later than the leak. The abandoned copies are already resident when the next prefill finishes and `_scatter_kv_cache` clones the new prefix into request-owned storage. That clone is the allocation that fails. The graph pool itself never grew to fill the card.

## Fix

Only the Qwen-Image-2.1 pipeline changes. The shared step runner already calls `pipeline.release_step_request` if the pipeline defines it; this PR implements that hook and does not touch the runner.

Before a prefill forward, `release_idle_entries()` drops every entry whose owner weakref is already dead. An owner that is still alive stays, so a concurrent request keeps replaying. There is no exception for the upcoming layout, batch size, or prefix length: the next request recaptures that key once. Keeping a dead entry for image layout alone would still stack copies when the prompt length or batch size changed.

The step path does this when the batch is still in prefill. The non-step `diffuse()` loop does it once, before the first forward. Both happen before the clone that was OOM'ing. `release_step_request` only clears that request's `kv_cache` and geometry. It does not touch the graph table; the next prefill is what drops the dead entry.

`empty_cache()` runs only when an entry was actually dropped, once per prefill, so the next clone can use the freed blocks. A repeated layout does not take that path.

## Test plan

- [x] CPU: `pytest -o addopts= tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_decode_graph.py::test_release_idle_entries_drops_dead_other_layouts tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21/test_request_geometry_lifecycle.py` — 10 passed. After the owners are dropped, every dead entry's static tensor is freed, including one that would match a later request, a live owner stays, `release_step_request` drops the request KV without clearing graphs, and non-step `diffuse` releases idle entries before the loop.
- [x] GPU, one card, two server processes. Each process serves every request below without restarting; the server is restarted only between the unpatched run and the patched run. Model `Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1`, the same serve flags as the issue, four synthetic PNGs with different aspect ratios (the report's images are not in this environment), `num_inference_steps=2`, `true_cfg_scale=1.0`. Two steps are enough: the static copy exists at the end of the first prefill, and the reported OOM is the next prefill's clone. Weights-loaded baseline was 33469 MiB both times.

| order | before end (MiB) | after end (MiB) |
|---|---:|---:|
| fixed, 1st | 51651 | 51319 |
| fixed, 2nd | 58711 | 58511 |
| shuffle 1 | 60357 | 51263 |
| shuffle 2 | 68863 | 51851 |
| shuffle 3 | 77353 | 51851 |
| shuffle 4 | 85843 | 52043 |

Unpatched, each new layout adds about 8.5 GiB and the fourth shuffle ends at 85843 MiB. Patched, the four shuffles end at 51–52 GiB. Each new request whose previous owner has finished logs one idle release with `remaining=0` before it captures again, including a repeated image order. Patched shuffle peaks were at most 60391 MiB, about 1.8 GiB above the fixed-order peak of 58511 MiB, and returned to ~52 GiB when the request finished.

- [x] `pre-commit run` on the five changed files passed (ruff, mypy, SPDX, forbidden imports, torch.cuda check).

issues.title: [Perf][Qwen-Image-2.1] Drop the unused text-encoder LM head
issues.body:
## Contributor intent (required human answers)

### 1. What outcome do you want to achieve?

Lower GPU memory use for Qwen-Image 2.1.

### 2. What is the highest-leverage variable for that outcome?

Resident weights, about 30 GiB of the ~37 GiB peak.

### 3. How will this work move that variable?

It drops 1.16 GiB of weights the pipeline never uses, and the output stays the same.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Users running Qwen-Image 2.1 on 24/32 GB GPUs are close to the limit, where about 1 GiB matters. Serving deployments get the headroom for batching or concurrency.

## Purpose

Related to #8586. I found it during the C2 cross-review. It is independent of #8680.

The pipeline only uses hidden states from the text encoder, but it runs the full `Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration`, so the unused LM head (1.16 GiB) stays on the GPU and computes logits that get thrown away. This replaces the head with `nn.Identity()` before the encoder moves to the GPU (Krea2 drops its vision tower the same way). The encoder is still called through its top-level forward, so the model-level CPU-offload hook on it keeps running.

The quantized text-encoder path (e.g. FP8) builds the same model, so it gets the same swap. Its weights stream through `load_weights`, so the checkpoint's `lm_head.weight` is dropped there with a `WeightsMapper`, as Boogu does (#7342).

## Test Plan

**vLLM Version:** 0.31.0

**vLLM-Omni Commit:** `5ce59dc5` + this PR

`pytest -q -m cpu tests/diffusion/models/qwen_image_21`, plus a BF16 A/B on 1× H200 (1024², 50 steps, seed 42; edit uses one reference image, `qwen_bear.png`).

## Test Result

CPU tests: 97 passed, including a new test that `load_weights` drops the text encoder's `lm_head.weight` (it fails without the mapper).

| | Peak allocated (GiB) | Latency (s/img) | Output |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| eager, T2I | 36.86 → 35.69 | 7.41 → 7.34 | identical |
| eager, edit | 36.87 → 35.70 | 8.51 → 8.43 | identical |
| default (compile + CUDA graph), edit | 39.01 → 37.84 | 6.91 → 6.86 | within run-to-run variation* |

Peak allocated drops by 1.17 GiB with graph decode and is unchanged without it, since the peak then falls in the DiT stage while the text encoder is on the CPU.

\* The default path is not bit-reproducible across processes even without this change: three base runs gave three different images (36.5–41.6 dB PSNR between them), and this PR vs base is 37.8–43.8 dB.

### 4. Whose customer or user needs does this address, and what are those needs?

Users and developers optimizing Qwen-Image-2.1 on Ascend A5 who need a reproducible, reversible fused FFN integration for further operator tuning and performance evaluation.

Before this change, Qwen-Image-2.1 uses main's native MLP, including its existing eligible in-place/pointwise optimizations. Preserve ND for Eagle's projections while leaving automatic NZ conversion available for other linears.
